scheme_name: Pipes Carrying Water From Source To Field-Pulses ISPOM
description:
The "Pipes Carrying Water From Source To Field-Pulses ISPOM" scheme is part of the Indian government's efforts to enhance irrigation facilities for pulse cultivation in the country.

This scheme was launched in 2021 under the Indian government's initiative to promote sustainable agriculture and improve food security.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide efficient irrigation facilities to pulse farmers.

The scheme aims to increase the area under pulse cultivation by ensuring timely and adequate water supply.

The target is to cover approximately 1 million hectares of land under pulse cultivation by the year 2025.

The scheme also aims to enhance the productivity of pulses by at least 20 percent within the same timeline.

The benefits of the scheme include the provision of pipes and irrigation infrastructure to farmers.

Farmers will receive financial assistance of up to INR 50,000 per hectare for the installation of pipes and irrigation systems.

The scheme specifically focuses on small and marginal farmers who are often the most affected by water scarcity.

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include farmers who own land specifically for pulse cultivation.

Farmers must have a landholding of not more than 2 hectares to qualify for the assistance.

The applicant must also be a registered farmer under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme.

Farmers must provide proof of land ownership and a valid Aadhar card during the application process.

The application process involves submitting an application form to the local agriculture department.

Farmers must also submit a project report detailing the proposed irrigation system.

The application form can be obtained from the local agriculture office or downloaded from the official government website.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local agriculture officer.

The officer will conduct a field visit to verify the details provided in the application.

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The disbursement is typically made within 30 days of approval.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The National Agricultural Development Programme oversees the operational aspects of the scheme.

Farmers can contact the local agriculture office for assistance and guidance regarding the scheme.

The scheme is expected to significantly improve the livelihoods of pulse farmers.

It is estimated that around 5 million farmers will benefit from this initiative.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 1,000 crore for the implementation of this scheme.

The scheme also aims to promote the use of modern irrigation techniques.

This includes the use of drip and sprinkler irrigation systems.

The initiative is expected to reduce water wastage by up to 30 percent.

The scheme aligns with the government's broader goal of achieving self-sufficiency in pulse production.

India currently imports about 30 percent of its pulse requirements.

The scheme is part of the larger National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm.

This mission aims to enhance domestic production of pulses and reduce dependency on imports.

The government has set a target to increase pulse production to 30 million tonnes by 2025.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable agricultural practices.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt water conservation techniques.

The use of organic fertilizers and pest management practices is also promoted.

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall agricultural growth in the country.

The government is also working on creating awareness about the benefits of pulses.

Pulses are an important source of protein for the Indian population.

The scheme is expected to improve nutrition levels among the rural population.

The government has partnered with various NGOs and agricultural organizations for effective implementation.

Regular training programs will be conducted for farmers to educate them about the scheme.

The scheme will also include monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to assess its impact.

Farmers will be encouraged to share their experiences and best practices.

The government aims to create a robust feedback mechanism for continuous improvement.

The scheme is expected to create job opportunities in rural areas.

It will also promote entrepreneurship among farmers.

The government plans to publish success stories of beneficiaries to inspire others.

The scheme is part of the government's commitment to doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The initiative is expected to enhance the resilience of farmers against climate change.

The scheme will also contribute to the sustainable development goals set by the United Nations.

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to maximize the benefits of the scheme.

The government will provide technical support to these cooperatives.

The scheme is expected to foster a sense of community among farmers.

The implementation of the scheme will be closely monitored by state governments.

Regular reports will be submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture.

The government aims to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation process.

The scheme is expected to be a game-changer for pulse farmers in India.

It will address the critical issue of water scarcity in agriculture.

The government is committed to ensuring that no farmer is left behind.

The scheme is a step towards achieving sustainable agricultural practices in India.

The government encourages farmers to take advantage of this initiative for their benefit.
